title: Joshua
lead: Moses' helper and successor, who fought Amalek, went partway up Sinai, spied out Canaan and led Israel across the Jordan into the land (Exodus 17; 24; Numbers 13–14; 27; the book of Joshua). His Hebrew name Yehoshua, shortened to Yeshua, became Iēsous in Greek, the same name as Jesus.

sections.b: Joshua son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, serves Moses from youth (Numbers 11:28). He is one of the twelve spies and, with Caleb, urges Israel to trust God and enter the land (Numbers 13:8, 16; 14:6–9). Moses lays hands on him before the people (Numbers 27:18–23; Deuteronomy 31:7–8; 34:9). In the book of Joshua he leads Israel across the Jordan, takes Jericho and divides the land, and at the end calls the tribes to choose whom they will serve: "I and my family will serve the LORD" (Joshua 24:15). Hebrews 4:8 says that Joshua did not give the people the final rest.
